methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a correct model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, then explain it again more clearly.
methodBriefing.why: Explaining the relationship and then repairing mistakes helps turn a short-lived understanding into a more usable one.
how: Read the model carefully.
Close it and explain the rule from memory.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix any missing step.
Explain it again in plain language without copying.
methodBriefing.completion: You can state the rule accurately, name the key step, and give a correct application.
personalization: Start with the big picture before details.
Use one step at a time.
If you miss, fix one step before trying again.

activities.label: Product rule overview
activities.title: Product rule model
activities.body: Read the model and note the main pattern.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a product by adding the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.

activities.label: Explain the product rule
activities.title: Product rule from memory
activities.body: Explain the rule in your own words. Then compare it to the model.
activities.correctAnswer: When differentiating a product, use the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A complete answer states the two-term pattern and applies it to a product. If you left out one term, repair that missing part next.

activities.label: Fix the product rule
activities.title: Repair the product rule
activities.body: Correct your explanation in one sentence.
activities.misconceptionSummary: A product is differentiated by changing only one factor.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate both factors: first derivative times second, plus first times second derivative.
activities.feedback: The correction must include both terms. If you only changed one factor, the rule is still incomplete.

activities.label: Chain rule overview
activities.title: Chain rule model
activities.body: Read the model and notice the two linked parts.

essentialIdeas: Differentiate a composite function by taking the derivative of the outer function and multiplying by the derivative of the inner function.

activities.label: Explain the chain rule
activities.title: Chain rule in plain words
activities.body: Explain the rule again without copying the model.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Only the outside function needs to be differentiated.
activities.correctAnswer: For a composite function, differentiate the outer function and multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both the outer derivative and the inner derivative. If you said only the outside changes, that leaves out the key link.

activities.label: Recognition check
activities.title: Choose the chain rule
activities.body: Pick the correct derivative rule.
choices: Differentiate the outer function and multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
Differentiate only the inner function and leave the outer function unchanged.
Differentiate both parts separately and add the results.
Multiply the two functions, then differentiate the product.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate the outer function and multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
activities.feedback: The chain rule links an outside derivative with an inside derivative. It is not the product rule, and it is not just differentiating one part alone.

items.essentialIdea: Product rule differentiates a product as f'g+fg' for two functions.

check.title: Differentiate a product
check.prompt: How do you differentiate the product of two functions f and g?
check.referenceAnswer: Use f'g + fg'. Differentiate the first function times the second, then add the first times the derivative of the second.
check.feedback: This is the two-term product rule, not a single derivative of the whole product.

items.essentialIdea: Chain rule differentiates a composite by multiplying outer and inner derivatives.

check.title: Differentiate a composite
check.prompt: How do you differentiate a composite function like f(g(x))?
check.referenceAnswer: Differentiate the outer function at the inner input, then multiply by the derivative of the inner function: f'(g(x))g'(x).
check.feedback: The outer derivative is evaluated at the inner function, then multiplied by the inner derivative.

recognitionCheck.title: Identify the chain rule
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which expression gives the derivative of a composite function f(g(x))?
recognitionCheck.feedback: That is the chain rule, which combines outer and inner derivatives.
